question:
Batch 80 cycle 2 = RULING 103, re-examined after cycle 1 (orchestrator 2026-11-14 '14:13', verbatim): "THE TARGETED RE-LISTEN (for a hold where the two independent readings differ on ONE number or name token, as '401k' against '401' on Blockware 06d34e15). The hold stands as the default: a number or name disagreement is never waved through. But one long-span reading against another is weak evidence about one token. Before the hold is final, BOTH recognisers are asked again on a SHORT window cut around that token alone (the token's word times, 1.5 s either side, the same audio the cut will use). The lock passes on that token only if BOTH short-window readings give the lock's token (after the canon, with the 401k fix: a plan's name is not the number 401000). If either short reading still differs, or the two differ from each other, the hold is final and the clip may only be saved by a variant that leaves the token out. Record both short readings on the pin." YOUR SIDE: "the re-listen lives in the pre-check service (adjudicate_lock's number / name class), with the canon-401k fix ... Must-fail tests: a real number disagreement ('68,000' against '86,000') still holds after the re-listen; '401k' against '401' passes only when both short readings say 401k."
Context: pipeline/lock_precheck.py is the pin-stage pre-check service: per segment it builds the render's own lock (pinned.segment_lock) on the acquired window, then RULING 72/84's comparison (as_spoken) of the lock against the second recogniser's (ElevenLabs scribe_v1) reading of the same words; a number / name / negation difference classes "hold". The decode runs under ONE GPU0 lease in serve_once; answer() runs after it is released. The render's own pinned stage does not run as_spoken (the builder seals the pre-check's verdict into the pin), so the render needs no change. pinned.py is an input of the pre-check's decoder sha (lock_precheck.py is not), so the rule itself (relisten_candidate, relisten_verdict, RELISTEN_PAD_S) lives in pinned.py and the I/O in lock_precheck.relisten.
The change: when as_spoken holds, lock_precheck.relisten asks pinned.relisten_candidate: exactly ONE difference in all, classed hold, the lock's side one token and the reading's at most one, a number or name (law L-v 2's _lv2_critical) and never a negation. Then the token's word times come from canon_spans over the lock's words (refused, hold, if the lock's words do not read as its text token for token); the window [start - 1.5, end + 1.5] is cut from the acquired window file (ffmpeg); the run's decoder (_whisper_transcribe) reads it under the GPU0 lease (a render first: LJ.render_wants_gpu0; a Gpu0Stop or an empty decode is outcome "error", no verdict, re-ask: never a pass and never a final hold); the second recogniser reads it; pinned.relisten_verdict passes only if BOTH readings' canon tokens contain the lock's token. A pass makes the verdict "same" (the lock's own token stands; the second reading is never adopted); a hold keeps the hold and names both readings in the reason. The entry records "relisten" {token, against, window, source_window, decoder_reading, second_reading, verdict, scribe_usd}; RULES adds "ruling 103" so older entries are never reused.
Tests: test_lock_precheck TestRuling103 (5) with fakes for both recognisers and the clip: 401k passes only with both short readings 401k (three hold cases); 68,000 against 86,000 holds unless both re-read 68,000; no re-listen for two differences, a negation or a content word; no GPU0 is "error"; the spend and RULES. The shared fixture now answers the short window (the decoder's video_id "relisten", the scribe's window.wav) with the long readings by default, so TestRuling84's number case re-listens and still holds. 41 passed; on the old pinned / lock_precheck the 5 fail on behaviour. Real data: on Blockware the decoder re-read "401k" and scribe "401" on 14.84-18.38 s, so the hold is final.
Cycle 1: qwen27b PASS; Grok's two findings were false on the code (no `if verdict != "adopt"` block exists; `spoken` is built after the re-listen sets "same", now pinned by an assertion: as_spoken.verdict "same" and spoken_text None on a pass); glm's notes not agreed: an error returns before the scribe call (never billed), and "the two differ from each other" is read on the TOKEN because the short window's edge words are cut mid-way and differ between recognisers (the real run: "IRA. ..." against "Roth IRA. ...").
FIND: anything cycle 1 missed: a fail-open (a number / name difference passing without BOTH short readings giving the lock's token); a re-listen outside the ruling's one-token number / name case; GPU0 used outside the lease or before a render; the second recogniser's word adopted on a pass; an error path that ends as a final hold or a pass. Only state what you can verify from the diff. Reply with the JSON verdict; keep the reasoning short; at most 3 findings.

rejected_findings.issue: The relisten's second-recogniser spend is appended to `spent` even when the decoder returned no words (error path), so the error re-ask's entry bills a scribe call whose reading is discarded; the ruling's error record carries no `scribe_usd` either, so the spend is unaccounted in the recorded evidence.
rejected_findings.fix: Move the scribe call (and `spent.append`) before the empty-decode check, or record `scribe_usd` on the error record; either keeps the spend attached to the reading that produced it.
